findings.title: getThreads now always sends a non-null serviceLevelAgreements object, which renders invalid SQL for every unfiltered call
findings.failure: Every MCP getThreads call that does not set slaStatuses or slaTypes (the default and the common case, including calls filtered only by status, assignee, labels etc.) fails with a Postgres syntax error, so the MCP thread listing tool is broken for all workspaces. The PR description's claim that an all-null serviceLevelAgreements object is a no-op in the DB layer is only true for the nested and/or/not EXISTS path, not the top-level path getThreads uses.
findings.fix: Follow the existing $surveyResponse pattern (getThreads.graphql:77,99): expose one nullable variable `$serviceLevelAgreements: ServiceLevelAgreementFilter = null` and pass `serviceLevelAgreements: $serviceLevelAgreements`, so the default is a null object that buildFilters skips. Separately, harden the API: make the builder at threadDbFilterUtils.ts:946 and :966 return rdsDbUtils.filtering.ignoreFilter() (`1 = 1`, packages/db/src/filtering.ts:10) instead of sql.fragment``, since a public API caller sending `serviceLevelAgreements: {}` hits the same error today. Add a createFilters unit test with `{ types: null, statuses: null, updatedAt: null }` asserting valid SQL.
findings.evidence: The operation hardcodes the object `serviceLevelAgreements: { statuses: $slaStatuses types: $slaTypes }` (getThreads.graphql:100-103), so the input is never null. threadsFilter.ts:58-72 parses it into `{types: null, statuses: null, updatedAt: null}` (non-null). determineThreadFilters.ts:178 passes it through unchanged. threadsQuery.ts → threadDb.ts:1179 createFilters → buildRecursiveFilters (threadDbFilterUtils.ts:1229 hasNonNullBaseFields is true because the object is non-null) → buildBaseFilterSql → rdsDbUtils.filtering.buildFilters (packages/db/src/filtering.ts:114-125), which calls the serviceLevelAgreements builder for any non-null value. That builder returns an empty fragment sql.fragment`` when all three fields are null (threadDbFilterUtils.ts:943-947). buildFilters keeps it (lodash compact keeps the truthy fragment object) and joins it with ` AND `; slonik 45.5.0 (packages/db/package.json:18) sql.join does not drop empty members. Result: alone it gives `()` via threadDbFilterUtils.ts:1278, so the WHERE is `t.workspace_id = $1 AND <scope> AND ()` (threadDb.ts:1252/1357); next to other filters it gives `a AND  AND b`. Both are syntax errors. The `!== null` all-null guard the PR relies on is the EXISTS path at threadDbFilterUtils.ts:647-649, which only runs for and/or/not branches via buildExistsRecursiveFilters. No test covers the all-null object (threadDbFilterUtils.test.ts:850-947 all set at least one field), and tools/graphql-lint/validateMcpOperations.ts only checks schema validity, so CI will pass.

findings.title: The 45 line SLA status selection is copied 12 times across three files instead of a per file fragment
findings.failure: About 540 near identical lines; the next schema change to ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetail (a new union member or field) has to be applied 12 times, and missing one silently gives agents an inconsistent shape between tools.
findings.fix: Define one fragment per file on the union, prefixed with the operation name the way getBroadcasts.graphql:109 (`fragment GetBroadcastsActor on InternalActor`) and getBroadcastDetails.graphql:122 do, e.g. `fragment GetThreadsSlaStatusDetail on ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetail { __typename ... }`, and use it for all four targets. Keep names unique across files because validateMcpOperations.ts concatenates every file into one document (UniqueFragmentNames).
findings.evidence: Diff adds the same six inline fragments under firstResponseTime, nextResponseTime, firstResolutionTime and totalResolutionTime in getThreads.graphql:174, getThreadDetails.graphql:96 and searchThreads.graphql:114 (12 copies of each `... on ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetail*` per the diff). The prefixed fragment convention already exists in 10 operation files (getBroadcasts, getBroadcastDetails, searchBroadcasts, etc.).

checked_fine: Every added field, type and enum is valid against packages/core-graphql/src/schema.ts: Thread.serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary (13932), the union and its six members with breachingAt/pausedAt/remainingMinutesAtPause/breachedAt/achievedAt/completedAt/cancelledAt (14057-14130), ThreadsFilter.serviceLevelAgreements: ServiceLevelAgreementFilter with types/statuses (6564, 6624), ServiceLevelAgreementType and ServiceLevelAgreementStatus enums

Deploy order: the field and filter already exist in the API; the MCP container fetches the live schema at startup (services/mcp-server/entrypoint.sh) and only the operation files change, so there is no API before MCP ordering and rollback is a redeploy of the previous image

Summary resolver cost: resolvers.ts:7761 returns all nulls without a query when tierId and serviceLevelAgreementPolicyId are both null; otherwise serviceLevelAgreementTrackerDataLoader batches per request (coreGraphqlDataloader.ts:912) into one workspace scoped DISTINCT ON query (serviceLevelAgreementTrackerDb.ts:131-158) covered by idx_sla_trackers_workspace_thread_type_created_at, so searchThreads first=50 adds one query, not 50

No field level permission gate on serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary or the tracker dataloader, so tokens that can read threads will not get a partial error that nulls the non-null summary and the parent thread
searchThreads parent is the full thread model (searchThreadsQuery.ts spreads result.result), so tierId and serviceLevelAgreementPolicyId are available to the summary resolver

Doc claim that slaStatuses can match an older BREACHED row while the summary shows the newest tracker matches the code: the filter is an EXISTS over all tracker rows (threadDbFilterUtils.ts:943-990) while the summary uses DISTINCT ON ... ORDER BY created_at DESC; types and statuses are ANDed within the same tracker row, matching the examples
getThreadDetails and searchThreads only add selections, no filter or variable changes, so they are not affected by the SQL issue
